key_insight: Private score estimation achieves a nearly minimax-optimal privacy–accuracy trade-off and enables diffusion models whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a theoretically grounded route to privacy-preserving generative modeling, with an implementation whose runtime is polynomial in sample size.
method: Represent scores with quadratic B-splines and sample an estimator using the exponential mechanism.
Implement private estimation via projected Langevin Monte Carlo.
Use the private scores in a suitably discretized diffusion model.
evidence_signal: The paper establishes error upper bounds and a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, and reports experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.
watch_item: Guarantees assume sub-Gaussian distributions with locally Hölder-continuous scores; polynomial runtime alone does not establish scalability in high dimensions.
paper_title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
